chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Ibn al-Nu'mayr, the freedman of al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Narrate to me about the male child, up to what age do the women wash him?' He said, 'Up to three years.'
ai.seo_question: At what age do women stop washing male children according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential limit for gender segregation in ritual purification, permitting women to wash a male child up to the age of three. In Shia fiqh, this age marks the transition from the stage of 'non-differentiation' (ghayr mukhannath) to distinct gender roles, influencing rules of hijab and marriageability (bulugh). The narration highlights the practical application of the Prophet's and Imams' guidance on maintaining modesty within the family structure.
